doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Self-taught, with stick-control lessons from Lee Young
summary: Hamilton says he was largely self-taught, took stick-control lessons from Lee Young, subbed for him, and could not read music but memorized Ellington and Lunceford records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Okay, let’s go back to your early training. Apparently this old man, as you said, he must have been hiring you so you’re working with him, but who was training you? Who trained you on your instrument? You said you bought a snare drum and then you say you had a drum set. There’s a big difference playing snare drum and drum set.
I’m more or less self-taught. I’m self-taught. I guess when I was about 15 or 16, I took lessons from Lee Young.
Prez’s brother.
Prez’s brother.
We interviewed him already too.
Lee?
Yeah, he’s funny.

Anyway, I started taking lessons from Lee because Lee was playing with Lorenzo Flennoy at the time, the band, with Red Callender, Lee, Red Mack, you know, those guys. Anyway I’m in high school and all of a sudden Lee had me to sub for him every now and then.
Because you had been studying with him, he knew you could handle it.
Well, you know, he taught stick controls.
Did he have you read out of books?
No, he didn’t teach me how to read.
So when you say stick control, is he working -­
Little (unintelligible).
So he’s working with you on a snare drum, he’s not working with you out of the kit?
No, just -­
So you’re just working technique and stick control.
Technique, yes.
But no reading?

Oh, no, I didn’t know how to read. I didn’t know how to read. I couldn’t read one note of music. Everything was here and here. I’d play an arrangement down, then one time I knew it. I had every record Duke had out. I had every record Jimmie Lunceford had out. And when Basie came out, when we heard Basie it really messed me up, man. Turned everybody around.
